newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Cinema blast injures 14 in southern Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Cinema blast injures 14 in southern Philippines.

text.p: Fourteen people were injured, four of them seriously, when a bomb exploded in a cinema in the southern Philippines on the eve of peace talks between the government and a Moslem guerrilla group, police said on Tuesday.
City police chief Julmunir Jubail said the blast occurred at around 7:00 p.m. (1100 GMT) on Monday evening inside a packed cinema in Iligan city on the southern island of Mindanao.
Most of the victims were injured in a stampede after the explosion, Jubail said, adding they were mostly college students.
One witness said there was a blinding flash of light in the balcony section of the cinema before the explosion.
Police said they suspected Moslem extremists seeking to disrupt peace negotiations were responsible.

The Philippine government and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) were due to meet on Tuesday in the town of Sultan Kudarat, south of Iligan city, to discuss ending more than 20 years of internal strife.
The MILF has been blamed for the deaths of more than 125,000 people in their war for greater autonomy.
Last year, the government signed a peace agreement with the mainstream Moro National Liberation Front.
